about: Austin's preconfigured landmarks, written as of 1986.

landmarks.name: Texas State Capitol
landmarks.text: The pink granite capitol of 1888, taller than the one in Washington, as every Texan will tell you. A new aluminium cast of the Goddess of Liberty was lifted onto its dome this June.

landmarks.name: UT Tower
landmarks.text: The 307-foot tower over the University of Texas, lit orange when the Longhorns win. A sniper shot 46 people from its observation deck in 1966; the deck has been closed since 1975.

landmarks.name: Congress Avenue Bridge
landmarks.find: Ann W. Richards Congress Avenue Bridge
landmarks.text: The bridge over Town Lake whose rebuilt crevices have drawn more than a million Mexican free-tailed bats. The city is trying to get rid of them; they pour out at dusk.

landmarks.name: Sixth Street
landmarks.text: Old Pecan Street's Victorian storefronts, packed with live music bars and blues clubs. Thursday to Saturday nights it is closed to cars and full of students.

landmarks.name: Barton Springs Pool
landmarks.text: A spring-fed pool in Zilker Park, 68 degrees all year and swum in since long before the city. Topless sunbathing is a local custom and a local argument.

landmarks.name: Zilker Park
landmarks.text: The city's big park along Barton Creek, with the Zilker moonlight tower that becomes a Christmas tree of lights every December. Kite festivals and frisbee all year.

landmarks.name: Driskill Hotel
landmarks.text: The 1886 Romanesque cattle-baron hotel on Sixth Street, where LBJ waited for his election results. Its mezzanine bar is thick with lobbyists when the legislature sits.

landmarks.name: Threadgill's
landmarks.text: The old gas station on North Lamar where Kenneth Threadgill's Wednesday hootenannies launched Janis Joplin. Chicken-fried steak and vegetables by the plate now.

landmarks.name: Austin City Limits Studio
landmarks.text: Studio 6A on the UT campus, where KLRU tapes Austin City Limits in front of a painted skyline backdrop. Stevie Ray Vaughan and Willie Nelson are regulars.

landmarks.name: LBJ Library
landmarks.find: Lyndon Baines Johnson Library and Museum
landmarks.text: The windowless travertine monument to Lyndon Johnson on the UT campus, with a replica of his Oval Office. Lady Bird keeps an office upstairs.

landmarks.name: Mount Bonnell
landmarks.text: The limestone lookout above Lake Austin, 102 steps up to the best sunset in town. A favourite of couples and legends.

landmarks.name: Treaty Oak
landmarks.text: The 500-year-old live oak where Stephen F. Austin is said to have signed a treaty with the Comanche and Tonkawa. The last of a grove called the Council Oaks.

landmarks.name: Robert Mueller Municipal Airport
landmarks.text: Austin's small airport, with jets landing low over East Austin's houses. A fight over building a bigger one somewhere else goes on.

landmarks.name: Frank Erwin Center
landmarks.text: UT's round arena by I-35, called 'the Drum', where the Longhorns play basketball and the big tours stop. Graduation fills it every May.

landmarks.name: Texas Memorial Stadium
landmarks.text: The Longhorns' football stadium on campus, where 80,000 burnt-orange fans fill the stands. Saturday afternoons in the fall stop the whole city.
